EXPLANATION: The strong carbonyl at 1699 cm⁻¹ and aromatic ring stretch at 1600 cm⁻¹ fit a benzaldehyde derivative. The cluster of bands at 1151–1231 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of aromatic C–F stretching, favoring a fluoro-substituted ring. The prominent out-of-plane C–H bends at 838 and 861 cm⁻¹ are consistent with para substitution on a benzene ring, matching p-fluorobenzaldehyde. The aromatic C–H stretch at 3081 cm⁻¹ further supports an aryl system; no strong C–Cl stretches (~700 cm⁻¹) are present to favor chloro derivatives.
